name: Pastel Violet
lede: Pastel Violet is a dusty, muted mauve fixed by the German RAL paint system in 1927 and also recorded twice more in the American ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955, under the separate names Argyle Purple and Charm School.

sections.title: Three names, one block
sections.body:
This color is RAL 4009 in the German RAL paint system, dated to 1927 [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary places the same swatch block (244, a pale reddish purple) under two further names: Argyle Purple, first recorded in 1912, and Charm School, both independent commercial names landing on the same block rather than copies of the RAL name [1]. This is common for pale, low-chroma colors: the color space runs out of room before the naming systems do [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[catalpa]], [[dove-grey]] and [[anemone]], at 2.6, 3.1 and 3.2 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this muted violet in 46 of 23,781 paintings, 0.19 percent, rarer than 58 percent of our named colors, as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 10 of 1,674 paintings, over three times the archive's baseline rate for that century, and most often sits as a mid-tone rather than a shadow or highlight [2]. The earliest dated example is a 1425 panel attributed to Sandro Botticelli, five centuries before RAL's 1927 record of the name, so the match is a look-alike hue, not a trace of any real pigment, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

questions.q: Besides Pastel Violet, what other two names does the ISCC-NBS dictionary give this same color block?
True or false: Argyle Purple and Charm School are both copies of the RAL name Pastel Violet.

openers: Pastel Violet shares its exact color block with two other names, Argyle Purple and Charm School, that have nothing to do with RAL.
